newsitem.title: USA: Cisco Systems buys Ardent, Global.
newsitem.headline: Cisco Systems buys Ardent, Global.

text.p: Cisco Systems, Inc., the world's largest supplier of Internet transmission equipment, said Tuesday it has agreed to buy privately-held Ardent Communications Corp. for about $156 million in stock.
Cisco also said it will buy Global Internet Software Group for about $40.25 million in cash, and take an undisclosed minority stake in the parent company, Global Internet.Com Inc.
Cisco expects to take one-time after-tax charges of 23 cents per share for the Ardent deal, and of 2 cents to 3 cents per share for the Global purchase.
Both definitive agreements are expected to close by late July.

Cisco and Sequoia Capital had previously held minority equity stakes in Ardent, a San Jose, Calif.-based maker of products for integrating voice, video and data on public or private computer networks.

Global Internet Software Group specialises in security solutions for Microsoft Windows NT networks. Global Internet.Com, whose principal investor is New York-based Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe, builds, manages and secures corporate networks with a focus on medium-size business.
Cisco's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $69.97 on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.
